how_title: Fifteen minutes. Your hands busy the whole time.
how_text: Every lesson is short enough for a coffee break and built from small, quick steps. No walls of grammar to scroll through — you learn by doing something every few seconds.
try_why_eres: “Eres” goes with tú. In Buenos Aires you say vos — and vos goes with sos.
try_why_estas: “Estás” is for how you are right now, not where you’re from. Try again!
try_note: Tap the word that finishes the question. In Buenos Aires it’s “vos sos”, not “tú eres”.
try_done: ¡Muy bien! ¿Vos de dónde sos? Here’s Lucho asking you the same thing.
steps_label: What you do in a lesson
step_choose_text: Pick the right word, form or reply — and see right away why.
step_match_text: Pair words with meanings, pictures and their porteño versions.
step_build_text: Put real phrases together tile by tile until word order feels natural.
step_listen_text: Every line is voiced in Rioplatense Spanish, so your ear learns the rhythm and the “sh” of the Río de la Plata.
step_roleplay_text: Order at a café, catch a bondi, chat with a neighbor — you answer, they reply.
step_speak_text: Say it out loud and check your pronunciation, if you turn on speaking practice.
cast_title: You just moved into a building in Palermo. Meet the neighbors.
cast_text: A1 follows your first weeks in Buenos Aires across 60 lessons. Lucho finds your keys on the stairs, Marta adopts you with an alfajor at her kiosco, Rubén keeps track of you in his famous cuaderno, and before long you’re hosting an asado on the terraza. Every new word comes with someone to say it to. Tap a neighbor to hear them.
cast_sofi_line: Hi! I’m Sofi, from 4B. What’s your name?
cast_ruben_line: Good afternoon! I’m Rubén, the building manager. What’s your name?
cast_marta_role: Runs the kiosco on the corner
cast_marta_line: Here, it’s dulce de leche. You’re family now!
cast_lucho_line: Great! On the pitch you learn everything… swear words too!
cast_caro_line: First day of work! Want a coffee?
scene_sub: It’s four in the afternoon. Rubén has been up since five. Sofi is just having breakfast.
scene_1: Sofi, it’s four in the afternoon. Are you only getting up now?
scene_2: No, Rubén! I get up at one. I have breakfast, I shower… and now, merienda!
scene_3: At one! I get up at five and sweep the sidewalk every day.
scene_4: And I draw until three in the morning. I work at night!
scene_5: Mili, Rubén’s granddaughter: So who’s right?
scene_reply_sofi: Very good! You’re a local now!
touch_text: Reminders arrive as messages from the neighbors: Spanish first, your language underneath. Practice today, and Marta might save you an alfajor.
touch_marta: Sweetheart! I saved you an alfajor and a lesson.
touch_lucho: Hey, training? Spanish, not fútbol. Okay, Spanish first.
touch_ruben: Sidewalk’s swept. Your turn now: one lesson.
rio_title: Textbook Spanish won’t get you through a Buenos Aires afternoon.
rio_text: Rioplatense is the Spanish of Buenos Aires and Montevideo. It has its own pronouns, its own sound and its own words. El Recreo teaches it from lesson one, instead of patching it on later.
rio_vos_text: Porteños use vos with its own verb forms. You’ll learn them as the default.
rio_vos_play: Play Lucho: Y vos, ¿tenés hermanos? (And you, do you have brothers and sisters?)
rio_sh_text: In Buenos Aires, ll and y sound like the English “sh”. Linguists call it yeísmo rehilado.
rio_sh_play: Play Sofi: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamás? (Hi! What’s your name?)
rio_words_text: Everyday expressions and a pinch of lunfardo, the city’s slang, with notes on when to use them.
culture_title: Real porteño life, not a phrasebook.
culture_text: Lessons are set where life in the city happens: sharing a mate, a Sunday asado, the corner kiosco, the colectivo across town. You pick up the language and the customs that come with it.

path_title: From your first “hola” to holding your own. A1 to C1.
path_text: Five levels, following the CEFR scale used by language schools and exams. A1 is complete: 10 units, 60 lessons, every line voiced. The next levels follow.
level_a1_text: Greetings, numbers, shopping, getting around — your first days in the city.
level_a2_text: Daily life and small talk: what you did, what you like, what you need.
level_b1_text: Live on your own terms: sort out problems, tell stories, keep a conversation going.
level_b2_text: Work, opinions and nuance — and the social codes behind them.
level_c1_text: Humor, idioms and the culture between the lines.

faq_rio_a:
It’s the Spanish spoken around the Río de la Plata — in Buenos Aires and Montevideo. Its best-known features are vos instead of tú (vos tenés, vos sos), the “sh” sound for ll and y (calle sounds like “ca-she”), a melodic, Italian-influenced intonation and plenty of local words, some from lunfardo, the city’s slang.

People from any Spanish-speaking country will understand you. You’ll just sound like you learned it in Buenos Aires.
faq_where_q: Where can I get El Recreo?
faq_where_a: On the App Store for iPhone, iPad and Mac, and on Google Play for Android.
faq_devices_q: Which devices does it run on?
faq_devices_a: iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android phones and tablets. On a Mac with Apple silicon, the iPad app installs from the Mac App Store and feels close to native. On Apple devices your progress syncs between them through your iCloud account. Progress doesn’t move between Apple devices and Android, and purchases are separate on each store.
faq_length_a: About 15 minutes. Each lesson is a series of short, hands-on steps — choosing, matching, building sentences, listening, role-playing a conversation and, if you like, speaking — so you’re doing something every few seconds instead of reading long explanations.
faq_beginner_q: I’m a complete beginner. Is it for me?
faq_beginner_a: Yes. The course starts at A1 with greetings and survival phrases. A1 is ready: 10 units and 60 lessons that follow your first weeks in a Buenos Aires building and its neighbors. If you already speak some Spanish, it’s a quick way to switch to how porteños actually talk.
faq_hear_q: Can I hear what it sounds like?
faq_hear_a: Yes. Every line in the course is voiced in Rioplatense Spanish, and the audio is built into the app, so it works offline. You can hear Sofi, Rubén and the other neighbors on the home page.
faq_languages_q: Which languages does the app speak?
faq_languages_a: The lessons teach Rioplatense Spanish, with explanations and translations in English, русский, português (Brasil), français or Deutsch. The app follows your device’s language.
faq_account_a: No. There’s no sign-up. Your progress is stored on your devices and synced through your own iCloud account. You pick a character, Alex or Sara, so the story can greet you, and that choice stays on your devices too. See the privacy policy for details.
faq_mic_q: Do I have to use the microphone?
faq_mic_a: No. Speaking exercises are optional and only use the microphone if you allow it. Your voice is not recorded or sent to us.
faq_cost_a: The first two units are free. After that, each level is a one-time in-app purchase — no subscription — and you can restore it on all your devices with the same Apple ID or Google account. Prices are shown in the App Store and Google Play. Nothing is sold on this website.
